item.content:encoded:
Change of commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-07-24

On 21 July, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced the dismissal of General Oleksandr Syrskyi as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) and the appointment of General Mykhailo Drapatyi, Commander of the Joint Forces, to replace him (see the profile in the Appendix). The reshuffle came against the backdrop of protests that began on 16 July in response to the removal of Mykhailo Fedorov as Minister of Defence, drawing crowds ranging from several thousand to over 10,000 people in Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities. The demonstrators primarily demanded the reinstatement of the popular minister and the dismissal of Syrskyi, who had been at odds with Fedorov.

President Zelensky made the decision after consulting representatives of a significant part of the military leadership. He held several meetings with Air Assault Forces Commander Oleh Apostol and also spoke with Deputy Chief of the AFU General Staff General Volodymyr Horbatiuk, Joint Forces Commander Mykhailo Drapatyi and corps commanders, including Generals Andrii Biletskyi, Ihor Obolenskyi and Denys Prokopenko.

The appointment of General Drapatyi, who enjoys broad public support and is held in high regard within the armed forces, aims to quell public discontent while preserving order and cohesion within the military. item.content:encoded:
Franco-German deterrence exercises and defence cooperation planning

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-07-24

On 17 July, Nörvenich Air Base in Germany hosted a meeting of the Franco-German Defence and Security Council, co-chaired by President Emmanuel Macron and Chancellor Friedrich Merz. The meeting took place ahead of the joint session of the French and German Cabinets in Brühl. The conclusions reaffirmed the two countries’ shared position on the wars in Ukraine and Iran and included commitments to deepen military cooperation, including joint exercises involving the Franco-German Brigade and the Multinational Corps Northeast in Szczecin, as well as defence-industrial cooperation, for example on long-range ballistic strike capabilities under the ELSA project. These commitments reflect the need for European states to assume greater responsibility for NATO’s collective defence. The two sides also pledged to develop capabilities in the space and cyber domains, including through the Joint Early Warning for a European Lookout (JEWEL) initiative and the use of French launch vehicles to place German satellites into orbit.

Nörvenich also hosted the first Franco-German exercises conducted under Macron’s forward deterrence concept, announced in March this year (see ‘Sovereign, yet forward-oriented towards Europe: the evolution of France's nuclear deterrence doctrine’). item.content:encoded:
Change of government in Moldova: policy continuity and new challenges

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-07-24

On 22 July, Moldova’s new government was sworn in, with independent businessman Vasile Tofan, aged 44, appointed as prime minister (see Appendix: biographical note and composition of the government). The previous day, parliament approved his government through a vote of confidence. The government’s programme and composition received support from 53 MPs representing the ruling pro-Western Party of Action and Solidarity (PAS), which is effectively led by President Maia Sandu. Opposition deputies either voted against the government or abstained. In his inaugural address, Tofan identified economic recovery through structural reforms and investment attraction as the government’s primary objective. He named the acceleration of European integration as the second key objective, aiming to conclude Moldova’s EU accession negotiations by 2028 and secure membership in 2030. Tofan also committed to continuing the reforms initiated by the previous cabinet, including fiscal and administrative-territorial reform.However, a couple of days before delivering his policy address, he stressed that these measures would be less extensive than previously proposed in order to avoid undermining PAS’s electoral prospects ahead of the 2029 parliamentary election.
